blocks.instruction: Leia o texto e escolha a alternativa correta. Algumas perguntas pedem inferência — a resposta não está escrita com todas as letras.
blocks.passage:
Demand and supply are the two sides of every supply chain. Demand is how much customers want. Supply is how much the company can provide. When they match, all is well.

When they do not match, problems begin. If demand is bigger than supply, the shelves go empty and customers leave. If supply is bigger than demand, the company is stuck with stock. That stock costs money, and it may never sell.

So the whole job of supply chain planning is simple: keep the two in balance. A good plan helps demand and supply match.

items.q: What is demand?
options: How much the company can provide
How much money the company has
How much stock is in the store
items.why: "Demand is how much customers want."

items.q: What happens when demand is bigger than supply?
options: The shelves go empty and customers leave
The company has too much stock
items.why: "If demand is bigger than supply, the shelves go empty and customers leave."

items.q: What is the main job of supply chain planning?
options: To keep demand and supply in balance
items.why: "the whole job of supply chain planning is simple: keep the two in balance."

items.q: The text suggests that too much stock is…
options: a problem, because it costs money
items.why: Inferência: o texto diz que o estoque custa dinheiro e pode nunca vender — logo, é um problema.

items.q: The author would most likely AGREE that…
options: balance between demand and supply is the goal
empty shelves are good for the company
supply is more important than demand
items.why: Inferência: o texto inteiro defende manter demanda e oferta em equilíbrio.

blocks.instruction: Ouça Sophie orientando uma nova planejadora. Responda sem ler a transcrição — ela só aparece depois de corrigir.

audio.text:
Welcome to the team. Today I want to talk about one number: your forecast.

Your forecast is how much you think customers will buy. It is the most important number in the whole system. Why? Because everything starts here. If your forecast is good, we make the right amount. If it is too low, the shelves go empty and customers go to a competitor. If it is too high, we make too much, and we must store stock that costs money.

So take your time with it. Look at last year. Look at what customers are doing now. Ask questions. That's why we sit together every week.

Remember: demand and supply must match. Your job is to guess demand as well as you can, so the company can plan supply. A good forecast keeps the two in balance. A bad one breaks it. You will make mistakes, and that is fine. Just learn from them.
audio.label: Ouça quantas vezes precisar. A transcrição aparece depois de corrigir.

items.q: What is a forecast, according to Sophie?
options: How many people work in the team
How much you think customers will buy
How much money the company makes
How much stock is in the store
items.why: "Your forecast is how much you think customers will buy."

items.q: What happens if the forecast is too high?
options: The company makes too much and must store stock
items.why: "If it is too high, we make too much, and we must store stock that costs money."

items.q: Why does the team sit together every week?
options: To look, ask questions and improve the forecast
items.why: "Look at last year. Look at what customers are doing now. Ask questions. That's why we sit together every week."

items.q: What does Sophie think about mistakes?
options: They are fine, if you learn from them
items.why: Inferência: "You will make mistakes, and that is fine. Just learn from them."

items.q: Why does Sophie call the forecast the most important number?
options: Because the boss asks for it
Because everything in the system starts with it
Because it is the biggest number
Because it is easy to make
items.why: Inferência: "everything starts here" — todo o resto do sistema depende do forecast.

blocks.instruction: O vocabulário da lição aparece aqui em frases novas. Escolha o sentido ou a palavra que cabe no contexto.

items.q: "When demand is high, many people want to buy." Demand means…
options: how much the company can make
items.why: Demand = demanda: quanto os clientes querem comprar.

items.q: Choose the correct word: "We must ___ demand and supply, so neither is too big."
items.why: To balance = equilibrar os dois lados.

items.q: Choose the correct word: "The ___ went empty, so customers could not find the product."
items.why: Shelf = prateleira; ela fica vazia quando falta produto.

items.q: "We have too much stock in the warehouse." Stock means…
options: the goods the company keeps to sell
items.why: Stock = estoque: os produtos guardados para vender.

items.q: Choose the correct word: "A ___ is another company that sells the same thing."
items.why: Competitor = concorrente: outra empresa que vende o mesmo produto.

blocks.instruction: Expressões que aparecem em reuniões de planejamento. Escolha o sentido no contexto.

items.q: "The manager must sign off on the forecast before we start." To sign off on means to…
items.why: Sign off on = aprovar formalmente, dar o aval.

items.q: "We will roll out the new plan next month." To roll out means to…
options: start using it, step by step
items.why: Roll out = implementar, colocar em prática aos poucos.

items.q: "Sales are down, so we need to keep an eye on demand." To keep an eye on means to…
items.why: Keep an eye on = ficar de olho, acompanhar com atenção.

items.q: "If demand goes up, we may run out of stock." To run out of means to…
items.why: Run out of = ficar sem, acabar o estoque.

items.q: "A new competitor can drive up or drop demand fast." To drive up means to…
items.why: Drive up = fazer subir, aumentar.
